plate_findings.evidence: Skin-coloured monomorphic papules on central face, forehead and nose with protruding central whitish spines

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A shows central face with monomorphic papules and central white spines, classic for trichodysplasia spinulosa, in article titled Trichodysplasia Spinulosa with matching caption and in-text description. B: Close-up panel B visibly shows follicular papules with white central spines on nose/central face, classic manifestation of trichodysplasia spinulosa per caption.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). B: Panel B is higher magnification H&E showing irregular outer root sheath with perinuclear eosinophilic/basophilic trichohyalin-type viral changes of trichodysplasia spinulosa.

in_text_mentions: Histopathological examination of one of the papules showed dilated follicular infundibulae with keratin plugs and viral-like changes with large irregular eosinophilic/basophilic trichohyalin-like granules within the inner root sheath cells consistent with TS [Figure 2]. Additional tests such as electron microscopy or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) were not performed.

A 3-mm skin punch biopsy of the nose revealed dilatation and keratotic plugging of vellus hair infundibula, with dystrophic expansion of the inner root sheath and absence of hair shafts. Viral polymerase chain reaction studies on the biopsy tested positive for TSPyV. plate_findings.evidence: disruption of the normal follicular maturation

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A 100x punch biopsy from back lesion in 63yo with VATS showing distorted follicle and trichohyalin granules consistent with trichodyplasia spinulosa. B: Panel B 400x higher magnification of same biopsy showing abnormal follicular maturation and trichohyalin inclusions of trichodyplasia spinulosa.
panels.attribution_text: Choi et al. A rare case of viral-associated trichodysplasia spinulosa in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.. International journal of women's dermatology 2023. doi:10.1097/jw9.0000000000000069. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Pathological findings of viral-associated trichodysplasia spinulosa showing unusual prominent trichohyalin granules with disruption of the normal follicular maturation showing basophilic inclusions within the follicular ostia, shown at magnification 100× (A) and 400× (B).
in_text_mentions: A 63-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of multiple reddish-pinkish papules on her face in the setting of long-standing CLL. Physical examination also showed leonine facies, superciliary madarosis, and an infiltrative nose. Many spiny red papules and spicules were located on her face, neck, chest, arms, and back (Fig. 1A and B). A punch biopsy of one of the lesions on the back revealed prominent trichohyalin granules with disruption of the normal follicular maturation showing basophilic inclusions within the follicular ostia consistent with VATS (Fig. 2A and B).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Panel A is facial clinical photo from case with biopsy-compatible Trichodysplasia Spinulosa; shows follicular papules with central keratin spines consistent with facial spicules. B: Panel B is second facial view of same patient with folliculocentric spikes, attributed to Trichodysplasia Spinulosa by biopsy and article title. C: Chest panel of same biopsy-confirmed Trichodysplasia Spinulosa case showing same follicular papules with keratin spine morphology; uses available spicule vocabulary with body_site chest and proposes truncal term for site difference. D: Extremity panel of same case showing follicular papules with spines; same disease attribution, site-specific proposal for extremity location. E: Close-up facial/beard skin showing prominent folliculocentric keratin spikes, classic for Trichodysplasia Spinulosa in this biopsy-compatible case.
